response.text: {"findings":[{"level":1,"severity":"blocking","kind":"definitional","finding":"Control theta appears directly in dcq/dt via delta×(1−theta)×c and the level measures the quitters compartment’s own peak, so the observed reduction is definitional and follows from the model definition rather than a paper finding.","suggestion":"Keep adherence control but change What-if to adherence 0.55 and measure R0 or peak of acutely infected I to test the paper’s >52% adherence threshold for R0<1.","term":"delta × (1 − theta) × c","claim":null},{"level":3,"severity":"blocking","kind":"definitional","finding":"Control eta appears directly in dr/dt via eta×r2×i and the level measures recovered’s own peak, so the increase is definitional and follows from the model definition.","suggestion":"Use rate of leaving acute stage r2 as control and test a joint increase of r2 with adherence on R0 or peak of I to reflect the paper’s synergistic recovery-adherence effect.","term":"eta × r2 × i","claim":null},{"level":4,"severity":"blocking","kind":"definitional","finding":"Control rho appears directly in dcq/dt via alpha×rho×cq and the level measures quitters’ own peak, so the decrease is definitional and follows from the model definition.","suggestion":"Measure R0 or peak of acutely infected I instead of quitters peak and test rho≈0.19 to illustrate the paper’s claim that chronic recovery rate pushes R0 below 1.","term":"alpha × rho × cq","claim":null},{"level":5,"severity":"blocking","kind":"definitional","finding":"Control delta appears directly in dcq/dt via delta×(1−theta)×c and the level measures quitters’ own peak, so the effect is definitional and follows from the model definition.","suggestion":"Change What-if to test adherence threshold on R0 or peak of I, e.g., adherence 0.55 reduces R0 below 1, rather than measuring the definitional quitters peak.","term":"delta × (1 − theta) × c","claim":null}]}
